## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sukhavihārijātaka* (Ja 10) is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. According to its traditional introductory narrative (*nidāna*), the Buddha recounted the story while residing at the Anupiya Mango-grove near Anupiya, occasioned by the Elder Bhaddiya (the Happy) [SuttaCentral]. Bhaddiya had renounced worldly life alongside five other Sakyan nobles and the barber Upāli; among them, Bhaddiya, Kimbila, Bhagu, and Upāli subsequently attained arahantship, Ānanda attained stream-entry, Anuruddha gained the divine eye, and Devadatta achieved supernormal powers [SuttaCentral]. The text opens with the thematic verse reflection beginning “The man who guards not,” and refers the detailed background of the six nobles leading to Anupiya to the *Khaṇḍahāla-jātaka* [SuttaCentral].

In terms of parallels and textual reuse, SuttaCentral identifies a passage-level parallel to the verses of the Elder Saṅkicca in the Theragāthā (Thag 11.1, *Saṅkiccattheragāthā*) [SuttaCentral]. Automated analysis by DharmaNexus records internal Pali text reuse consisting of four shared passages (totaling 312 characters) with the prose *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Paṭhamo bhāgo), with the most substantial alignment spanning segments §2.1–4.1 against commentary segments §1090–1093 [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language parallels with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora are recorded above threshold [DharmaNexus]. Seven modern translations across five languages are indexed on SuttaCentral, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato entitled *One Who Lives Happily* [SuttaCentral].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
